title: Additive Effect of Highly Aspherical Lenslet Target Spectacles to Children Inadequately Controlled by Atropine Monotherapy

license.statement: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (article <license>: open access article under the CC BY-NC-ND license; © 2025 American Academy of Ophthalmology)

groups.description: group A: atropine 0.01% every night continued, plus Essilor Stellest highly aspherical lenslet target (HALT) spectacle lenses from baseline; children aged 6-11 years enrolled because they progressed by >=0.5 D over the 6 months before enrolment on low-dose atropine (pre-baseline enrolment criterion); Singapore National Eye Centre

group B: atropine 0.01% twice daily (n = 5) or atropine 0.025% every night (n = 25) continued, plus Essilor Stellest HALT spectacle lenses from baseline; no single atropine concentration, so atropine_percent is not given; same pre-baseline enrolment criterion as group A; Singapore National Eye Centre

cells.definition: definition:Table 1 'Change in AL (mm)' rows 'First 6 mos' and 'Over 12 mos' are changes from the baseline visit at the start of HALT lenses (Methods); change at baseline is 0

series.notes: mean (SD) as printed (the Results text gives the same statistic as mean +/- SD); one value per child, eye basis not stated (multivariate GEE analyses used both eyes), used as tabulated; IOLMaster 500; all 20 children seen at 6 and 12 months; 'Second 6 mos' interval change not used

notes: Prospective cohort, Singapore National Eye Centre; children enrolled because they progressed by >=0.5 D in the 6 months before enrolment while on low-dose atropine; HALT lenses added at baseline while atropine continued. The selection is an enrolment criterion measured before the tabulated baseline, not an outcome of the tabulated follow-up.
The Results text quotes 12-month and second-6-month AL figures that do not all match Table 1; the Table 1 cells are cited.
Refraction (cycloplegic SE) and pupil size are tabulated but are not axial length.
